```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(targets)

work <- tar_read(work_scale)
flow <- tar_read(dataset_flow)
measured <- tar_read(measured)
pooled <- tar_read(screen_pooled)
units <- tar_read(described_units)
week <- tar_read(described_week)
relations <- tar_read(described_relations)
outcomes <- tar_read(described_outcomes)
trends <- tar_read(screen_trends)
trends_share <- tar_read(screen_trends_share)
manifest <- tar_read(data_manifest)
settings <- tar_read(settings)
exposures <- tar_read(exposure_registry)

fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
num <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10))
stage_order <- settings$school_stage_labels
measure_labels <- c(
  total_screen = "Total screen time",
  st_watch = "Watching",
  st_game = "Gaming",
  st_socmedia = "Social media",
  st_educational = "Educational use",
  st_comp = "Computer",
  st_tablet = "Tablet",
  st_phone = "Phone",
  st_educontent_watch = "Educational programmes"
)
label_measure <- function(x) coalesce(measure_labels[x], x)
```

A working draft of the descriptive half of the report to the funder, built before any model is run.
Screen use and outcomes are described separately here: nothing relates one to the other.
Every figure is computed within each study's own waves and countries first, using survey weights where the study released them, and then pooled so that each dataset counts once; a figure needs `r settings$min_datasets` or more datasets.
No dataset is named.
Data: `r nrow(manifest)` datasets, overall hash `r unique(manifest$overall_hash)`.

## The scale of the work

```{r}
#| label: totals
work$totals |>
  transmute(` ` = item, Count = fmt(count)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lr")
```

```{r}
#| label: flow
flow |>
  mutate(across(c(datasets, participants, rows), \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", fmt(x)))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Stage", "Datasets", "Participants", "Observations"), align = "lrrr", caption = "Datasets from specification to analysis. Datasets identified or requested but never specified are not recorded in the repository.")
```

```{r}
#| label: files
work$files |>
  filter(role == "data") |>
  transmute(Format = reader, Datasets = datasets, Files = fmt(files)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr", caption = "Raw data files read, by format.")
```

```{r}
#| label: mapping
status_labels <- c(
  compatible = "Compatible: converts to the shared variable without loss",
  partial = "Partial: part of the construct, or a simplification",
  proximate = "Proximate: a close but not equivalent set of categories",
  inferred = "Inferred: from the study's design or documentation",
  incompatible = "Incompatible: related information exists but cannot be used",
  unavailable = "Unavailable: the study did not collect it",
  in_progress = "Not yet decided"
)
work$mapping |>
  mutate(order = match(status, names(status_labels))) |>
  arrange(order) |>
  transmute(`Mapping decision` = coalesce(status_labels[status], status), `Variable-by-dataset decisions` = fmt(rows), Datasets = datasets) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr", caption = "Every shared variable was considered for every dataset, and the decision recorded with its reason.")
```

```{r}
#| label: schema
work$schema |>
  arrange(desc(rows)) |>
  transmute(Domain = domain, `Shared variables` = rows) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lr")
```

## Who is in the data

```{r}
#| label: who
tibble::tibble(
  ` ` = c("Datasets", "Countries", "Collection years", "Waves and countries analysed separately (units)", "Datasets that follow the same children over time", "Units with survey weights"),
  Value = c(
    n_distinct(units$dataset_id),
    n_distinct(na.omit(units$country)),
    paste(round(min(units$year, na.rm = TRUE)), "to", round(max(units$year, na.rm = TRUE))),
    fmt(nrow(units)),
    n_distinct(units$dataset_id[units$repeats_participants]),
    paste0(fmt(sum(units$weighted)), " (", pct(mean(units$weighted)), ")")
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-year-age
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Observations by collection year and median age of the unit. Each cell sums the observations of the units that fall in it."
units |>
  filter(!is.na(year), !is.na(age_median)) |>
  mutate(year = 5 * floor(year / 5), age = 2 * floor(age_median / 2)) |>
  summarise(rows = sum(rows), datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = c(year, age)) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, age, fill = rows)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = datasets), size = 2.5, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", labels = scales::comma, name = "Observations") +
  labs(x = "Collection year (five-year bands)", y = "Median age of the unit (two-year bands)", caption = "Numbers are datasets.")
```

```{r}
#| label: countries
units |>
  mutate(country = coalesce(country, "(not recorded)")) |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), rows = sum(rows), .by = country) |>
  arrange(desc(datasets), desc(rows)) |>
  head(20) |>
  transmute(Country = country, Datasets = datasets, Observations = fmt(rows)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr", caption = "The 20 countries with most datasets.")
```

## What was measured

### Screen use

```{r}
#| label: measured-exposures
measured$exposures |>
  filter(day == "usual", context == "any") |>
  mutate(kind = c(activity = "Activity", device = "Device", subset = "A subset of an activity", aggregate = "Aggregate")[axis]) |>
  transmute(Measure = exposure, Kind = kind, Datasets = datasets, `Dataset-waves` = dataset_waves, Observations = fmt(observations)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "Usual-day screen measures, by how many datasets hold them.")
```

```{r}
#| label: how-measured
units |>
  filter(!is.na(measure_type)) |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), units = n(), rows = sum(rows), .by = c(measure_type, responder)) |>
  arrange(desc(rows)) |>
  transmute(`Response format` = measure_type, `Who reported` = coalesce(responder, "(not recorded)"), Datasets = datasets, Units = units, Observations = fmt(rows)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "How screen use was asked: response bands (categorical) against open entry (continuous), and who answered.")
```

### Outcomes

```{r}
#| label: measured-outcomes
measured$outcomes |>
  transmute(
    Family = prereg_family,
    `Specific outcome` = label,
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Dataset-waves` = dataset_waves,
    Observations = fmt(observations),
    `Shared variables` = schema_rows,
    Informants = informants,
    `Score types` = score_types
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrll")
```

## How much children use screens

Medians and shares lead, because response bands with an open top make means understate heavy use.
The middle column is the median dataset's value; the range is the middle half of datasets.

```{r}
#| label: distributions
usual <- exposures$variable_name[exposures$day %in% "usual"]
pooled |>
  filter(grouping == "all", variable_name %in% c(usual, "total_screen")) |>
  arrange(variable_name != "total_screen", desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(
    Measure = label_measure(variable_name),
    `How built` = built,
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Median hours a day` = paste0(num(median_mid), " (", num(median_low), " to ", num(median_high), ")"),
    `Reporting none` = paste0(pct(share_zero_mid), " (", pct(share_zero_low), " to ", pct(share_zero_high), ")"),
    `2 hours or more` = paste0(pct(share_2plus_mid), " (", pct(share_2plus_low), " to ", pct(share_2plus_high), ")"),
    `4 hours or more` = paste0(pct(share_4plus_mid), " (", pct(share_4plus_low), " to ", pct(share_4plus_high), ")")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrr")
```

Total screen time is shown by how it was built, and the rows are not comparable with each other: a sum of more content classes is larger because more was asked.

```{r}
#| label: fig-by-stage
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Median hours a day by school stage: the median dataset (point) and the middle half of datasets (line). Numbers are datasets."
pooled |>
  filter(grouping == "school_stage", variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational")) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = stage_order), measure = label_measure(variable_name)) |>
  ggplot(aes(group, median_mid)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = median_low, ymax = median_high), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(label = datasets, y = median_high), vjust = -0.6, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Median hours a day") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: by-sex-ses
pooled |>
  filter(grouping %in% c("sex", "ses_household"), group %in% c("Female", "Male", "Low", "Medium", "High"), variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational")) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Female", "Male", "Low", "Medium", "High"))) |>
  arrange(variable_name, group) |>
  transmute(
    Measure = label_measure(variable_name),
    Group = group,
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Median hours a day` = paste0(num(median_mid), " (", num(median_low), " to ", num(median_high), ")"),
    `2 hours or more` = paste0(pct(share_2plus_mid), " (", pct(share_2plus_low), " to ", pct(share_2plus_high), ")")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "By sex, and by household socioeconomic position relative to the study's own sample.")
```

## Weekdays and weekends

Compared on the same children, where a study asked both.

```{r}
#| label: week
week |>
  summarise(
    weekday = weighted.mean(mean_weekday, n),
    weekend = weighted.mean(mean_weekend, n),
    more = weighted.mean(share_more_on_weekend, n),
    .by = c(dataset_id, exposure)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    datasets = n(),
    weekday = median(weekday),
    weekend = median(weekend),
    more = median(more),
    .by = exposure
  ) |>
  filter(datasets >= settings$min_datasets) |>
  arrange(desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(Measure = exposure, Datasets = datasets, `Mean hours, weekday` = num(weekday), `Mean hours, weekend day` = num(weekend), `Share using more on a weekend day` = pct(more)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

## Change over time

Estimated inside each repeated survey and then pooled, because comparing periods across datasets mixes real change with which datasets exist in each period.
Studies that follow the same children are left out: there the year moves with the children's age.
Only `r n_distinct(trends$slopes$dataset_id)` datasets are repeated surveys with three or more collection years, so this section is thin.

```{r}
#| label: trend-table
trend_table <- function(trend, unit_label) {
  if (is.null(trend$pooled) || nrow(trend$pooled) == 0) return(NULL)
  trend$pooled |>
    transmute(
      Measure = label_measure(variable_name),
      Datasets = datasets,
      Years = paste(first_year, "to", last_year),
      Change = paste0(num(change_per_decade), " (", num(ci_low), " to ", num(ci_high), ")")
    ) |>
    knitr::kable(align = "lrlr", col.names = c("Measure", "Datasets", "Years", paste(unit_label, "per decade (95% interval)")))
}
trend_table(trends, "Change in mean hours a day")
```

```{r}
#| label: trend-share
trend_table(trends_share, "Change in the share at 2 hours or more")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-trend
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Mean hours a day by collection year within each repeated survey. Each line is one dataset, unlabelled."
trends$series |>
  filter(variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_watch_wd", "st_game", "st_game_wd", "st_socmedia", "total_screen")) |>
  mutate(measure = label_measure(sub("_wd$", "", variable_name)), day = ifelse(grepl("_wd$", variable_name), "weekday", "usual day")) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, value, group = interaction(dataset_id, variable_name), linetype = day)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Collection year", y = "Mean hours a day", linetype = NULL)
```

## How the kinds of screen use relate

Rank correlations between two screen measures among the same children, within each unit.

```{r}
#| label: relations
relations |>
  summarise(rho = weighted.mean(spearman, n), both = weighted.mean(share_both, n), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_a, variable_b)) |>
  summarise(datasets = n(), rho = median(rho), low = quantile(rho, 0.25), high = quantile(rho, 0.75), both = median(both), .by = c(variable_a, variable_b)) |>
  filter(datasets >= settings$min_datasets) |>
  arrange(desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(`Measure` = label_measure(variable_a), `With` = label_measure(variable_b), Datasets = datasets, `Rank correlation` = paste0(num(rho), " (", num(low), " to ", num(high), ")"), `Share doing both` = pct(both)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
```

## Binary outcomes

Prevalence within each unit, pooled so that each dataset counts once.
Standardised scores are not shown, because they carry no meaning on their own.

```{r}
#| label: outcomes
outcomes |>
  filter(grouping == "all") |>
  summarise(prevalence = weighted.mean(prevalence, n), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name)) |>
  summarise(datasets = n(), mid = median(prevalence), low = quantile(prevalence, 0.25), high = quantile(prevalence, 0.75), .by = variable_name) |>
  filter(datasets >= settings$min_datasets) |>
  arrange(desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(Outcome = variable_name, Datasets = datasets, Prevalence = paste0(pct(mid), " (", pct(low), " to ", pct(high), ")")) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-outcomes-stage
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Prevalence by school stage for the binary outcomes with most datasets: the median dataset (point) and the middle half (line)."
by_stage <- outcomes |>
  filter(grouping == "school_stage") |>
  summarise(prevalence = weighted.mean(prevalence, n), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name, group)) |>
  summarise(datasets = n(), mid = median(prevalence), low = quantile(prevalence, 0.25), high = quantile(prevalence, 0.75), .by = c(variable_name, group)) |>
  filter(datasets >= settings$min_datasets)
top <- by_stage |> summarise(k = max(datasets), .by = variable_name) |> slice_max(k, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE)
by_stage |>
  filter(variable_name %in% top$variable_name) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = stage_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(group, mid)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(vars(variable_name), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Prevalence") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```
